summary.headline: Raymond Lifestyle FY26 total income hit record INR7,034 crore (+11% YoY) and EBITDA rose 23% to INR804 crore; Q4 EBITDA up 53% to INR152 crore.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a recovery year, with record annual total income of INR7,034 crore (+11% YoY) and EBITDA of INR804 crore (11.4% margin, +23%). Q4 FY26 total income was a record INR1,810 crore (+15% YoY), with EBITDA up 53% to INR152 crore and margin up 210 bps QoQ to 8.4%. The company remains debt-free with a net cash surplus of INR179 crore, and net working capital days fell from 87 to 77. Management labelled FY27 a "Year of Consolidation", guiding to double-digit top-line and bottom-line growth without numeric EBITDA guidance.

financial_highlights.change: Includes INR53 crore one-time subsidy in base year

segments.name: Branded Textile
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR831 crore (+14% YoY) on volume growth and premiumisation; EBITDA up 126% to INR115 crore on mix, volume, ASP and scale.

segments.name: Branded Apparel (reported, incl. emerging businesses)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR469 crore (+20% YoY) with double-digit like-for-like growth in retail; EBITDA INR19 crore, 5.4% margin excluding emerging businesses. Core four brands (Park Avenue, ColorPlus, Raymond Ready-to-Wear, Parx) had revenue INR1,667 crore at 7.8% EBITDA margin; emerging businesses are about INR140 crore annual revenue with about INR30 crore loss.

segments.name: Garmenting (exports)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR342 crore vs INR248 crore (+38% YoY); EBITDA INR14 crore vs negative INR7 crore, margin 4.1%. March was the highest-ever monthly revenue; US share was about 65-67% and management wants to reduce it.

segments.name: High value cotton shirting (B2B)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR197 crore (+6% YoY); EBITDA INR20 crore vs INR61 crore last year, which included a INR53 crore one-time government subsidy for the Amravati plant.

guidance_outlook: FY27 is the 'Year of Consolidation': double-digit top-line and bottom-line growth targeted, with bottom-line growing faster than top-line; no numeric EBITDA guidance given.
Capex for FY27 similar to FY26 (about INR180 crore): about INR50 crore SAP, about INR60 crore new Hyderabad garmenting factory, balance for stores and maintenance.
Store network: about 100 gross EBO additions in FY27, 50-60 closures, net addition 30-40; network not to dip below 1,653 and expected near 1,700 at end of FY27.
Working capital target below 70 days in FY27 (about 8-9 days further reduction).
Core four apparel brands targeted to reach double-digit EBITDA margin over about two years from 7.8%.
Garmenting next year expected to be better; first-quarter order book reported as full and second-quarter order booking under way.
risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from rising Merino wool and flax prices offsetting premiumisation gains.
US tariff reversal risk (management cited possible return of 30-40% tariff) and concentration of garmenting exposure.
Store rationalisation and new-store productivity; net addition of only 30-40 stores in FY27.
Discretionary demand risk from West Asia conflict, high crude, heat waves and below-normal monsoon forecast.
Emerging businesses (about INR140 crore revenue, about INR30 crore loss) still weigh on Branded Apparel margins until separate reporting starts next quarter.
Branded Textile profitability has declined since FY23 despite flat-to-low growth; recovery path not quantified.
Management transition: new Group CFO, Lifestyle CFO, CEO and CMO; CIO search ongoing; three-year strategy consultant to deliver about October-November 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall from 54-55% to 51-52% in Q4, and are the opex and employee cost declines sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR53 crore subsidy sits in the base; ex-subsidy Q4 gross margin is about 44-45%, and FY26 gross margin is 44% including the subsidy. Q4 income grew 15% against opex growth of 1.2%, attributed to factory utilisation above 90% and lower garmenting labour and store-closure savings.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 store plan?
qa_highlights.answer: About 100+ gross store additions, 50-60 closures, net 30-40; no dramatic change in strategy in the consolidation year.

qa_highlights.question: How big are emerging and new businesses in Branded Apparel?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR140 crore annual revenue with about INR30 crore loss; core four brands would be at 7.5-8% margin after adding back these losses.

qa_highlights.question: Plans to reduce US dependence in garmenting and impact on margins and raw materials?
qa_highlights.answer: US share was about 65-66%; management is expanding to Europe and UK, citing better freight costs. Wool and flax supply are not disrupted, but Merino wool and flax prices are rising. Gross margin improvement expected to be modest.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for Branded Textile profitability, which has declined since FY23?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects low-to-medium single-digit segment growth, with value growth above volume through premiumisation, casualisation, tier-2/3 expansion, tailoring ecosystem support and export of fabric; sees a path back to older profitability levels over time, no numbers given.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital levers beyond FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Debtor overdue clamp-down and inventory actions; target below 70 days in FY27, another 8-9 days reduction from 77 days.

qa_highlights.question: Ethnix competitive intensity and growth strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is recalibrating Ethnix toward lighter wedding-guest products such as kurtas and bandis, distribution via TRS and Ethnix stores, and Indo-Western bandhgalas; no numeric growth given.

capex_capacity: FY27 capex expected broadly similar to FY26's about INR180 crore, per E.C. Prasad.
Of the about INR180 crore, about INR50 crore relates to SAP implementation and about INR60 crore to the new garmenting factory in Hyderabad; the balance is for new stores and plant maintenance.
Factory utilisation rose from a traditional 80-85% to above 90%, with some factories at 95%+, per CEO Satyaki Ghosh.
Store network: about 100 gross EBO additions in FY27 against 50-60 closures, net addition 30-40; network not to dip below 1,653 and expected near 1,700 at end of FY27.
S/4HANA implemented in the textile and home businesses; no store expansion push until strategy work completes, with decision on aggressive expansion closer to end of FY27.
demand_pricing: Q4 FY26 Branded Textile revenue INR831 crore (+14% YoY) on volume growth and premiumisation; management cited ASP growth and mix.

Branded Apparel Q4 revenue INR469 crore (+20% YoY) with double-digit like-for-like growth in retail channels; core four brands INR1,667 crore revenue at 7.8% EBITDA margin, targeted to reach double-digit in about two years.
Emerging and new businesses in Branded Apparel: about INR140 crore annual revenue with about INR30 crore loss; to be reported separately from next quarter.

Garmenting: Q4 revenue INR342 crore (+38% YoY); March was the highest-ever monthly revenue; US share about 65-67%, with a plan to diversify toward Europe and UK after UK FTA and EU FTA; Q1 FY27 order book described as full and Q2 order booking under way.

Gross margin FY26 about 44% including the INR53 crore base-year subsidy; management said Q4 gross margin ex-subsidy would be about 44-45%; Merino wool and flax price increases are a headwind to premiumisation gains.
Sleepwear exit removes an annual EBITDA drag of about INR20 crore, per management, though provisions were taken this year.
Working capital days fell from 87 to 77; target below 70 days in FY27.
key_quotes: FY26 has been a year of recovery for Raymond Lifestyle.
So, the core brands are actually quite okay at 7.8% and we will endeavour to take it to double-digits over the next two years' time.
As we enter FY '27, we would like to call this the Year of Consolidation.
So, our order books are solid.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 recovery and Garmenting order books, but cautious on FY27, framed as a 'Year of Consolidation' with no numeric EBITDA guidance. Management repeatedly hedged on raw material costs, West Asia conflict, discretionary demand and US tariff risk, and declined to give 3-5-10 year revenue targets pending a strategy consultant due around October-November 2026.

adds.what: New garmenting factory in Hyderabad (part of ~INR180 crore FY27 capex, ~INR60 crore allocated)
Net ~30-40 EBO store additions in FY27 (~100 gross adds, 50-60 closures); network to end FY27 near 1,700

growth.why: Management guides double-digit FY27 top-line growth (bottom line faster), backed by a full Q1 garmenting order book, ~90%+ factory utilisation, and a ~INR60 crore Hyderabad garmenting factory, though no numeric EBITDA guidance and store additions are only net 30-40.
